cards.text: The flood is over, and God has set His rainbow in the clouds as a sign (Genesis 9:13). Now meet the sons of Noah who came out of the ark: Shem, Ham and Japheth. And Ham was the father of Canaan.

cards.question: Shem, Ham and Japheth are Noah's three sons. From them, the whole ___ was populated.

cards.text: Now Noah, a man of the soil, gets to planting. This man is over 600 years old (Genesis 8:13), friend, and I still groan every time I step off my gold base.

cards.question: Noah the man of the soil gets to planting. What does he plant?

cards.text: Noah drinks some of its wine, becomes drunk and uncovers himself inside his tent. Oh, friend, this family just made it through a flood, and here comes trouble.

cards.question: Ham, the father of Canaan, sees his father's nakedness inside the tent. What does Ham do?

answers.text: He tells his two brothers outside
He covers his father with a cloak
He goes in and wakes his father

cards.text: Shem and Japheth take a garment and lay it across their shoulders. They're going to cover their dad, and they've got a plan.

cards.question: Shem and Japheth have the garment across their shoulders. How do they get to their father?
Shem and Japheth see their father's nakedness while they cover him.

cards.text: When Noah wakes up, he learns what his youngest son had done to him. And notice this: twice now, the text has called Ham the father of Canaan.

cards.question: Noah has learned what his youngest son did to him, and he speaks a curse. Who does Noah curse?
In his curse, Noah says Canaan will be a ___ to his brothers.

cards.text: Then Noah declares, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem!" Look close, friend: the one being blessed in that line is the LORD Himself.

cards.question: Right after blessing the LORD, the God of Shem, Noah says may Canaan be Shem's servant.
Noah has words for Japheth too: may God expand Japheth's ___.

cards.text: Then Noah adds, "may he dwell in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his servant." That's the third time in one speech Noah says Canaan will be a servant.
Noah isn't done yet, friend. This man's got more years left than I've got sprinkles, and I've got a LOT of sprinkles.

cards.question: After the flood, how many more years does Noah live?

cards.text: So Noah lives a total of 950 years, and then he dies.

Now comes the account of Noah's sons Shem, Ham and Japheth, who also had sons after the flood. Japheth's line goes first: Gomer, Magog, Javan and more. From these, the maritime peoples separated into their territories, by language and clan.
Next up is Ham's line: Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan. And Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one on the earth.

cards.question: Nimrod, son of Cush, began to be a mighty one on the earth. What is Nimrod known as?

cards.text: He's so known for it that it becomes a saying: "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD." Friend, nobody has EVER said "Like Dorin, a mighty stamper." Not out loud, anyway.

cards.question: Nimrod the mighty hunter has a kingdom. Where does his kingdom begin?
Once his kingdom begins in the land of Shinar, Nimrod stays there for good.
Nimrod goes from Shinar into Assyria, and there he builds the city of ___.

cards.text: The rest of Ham's line fills in fast. It includes the Philistines, the Hittites, the Jebusites and the Amorites, and Canaan's borders reach from Sidon as far as Gaza and toward Sodom and Gomorrah.

Last comes Shem, the older brother of Japheth. In his line, Eber has a son named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and Peleg's brother Joktan has THIRTEEN sons. I had six little cutters on one counter and thought THAT was a crowd.

cards.question: From the clans of Noah's sons, the ___ of the earth spread out after the flood.

findings.problem: Right before card 11 asks who Noah curses (Canaan, with Ham as a wrong answer), this card says 'twice now, the text has called Ham the father of Canaan.' That points the baker straight to Canaan and steers them off Ham, so it gives away the answer to the next card.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The 'twice now' line draws on Genesis 9:18 and 9:22, but the card cites only Genesis 9:24.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: No earlier card sets up Noah's words for Japheth. The card is the line of Genesis 9:27 with one word removed, so the baker has to guess the wording ('territory' vs 'flocks' vs 'wisdom') instead of reasoning out the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card says Noah three times 'says Canaan will be a servant.' Genesis 9:26-27 word two of the three as wishes ('May Canaan be…'), not statements. The line also calls it 'one speech,' but the text adds the second part with 'He also declared' (9:26).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The 'third time' count draws on Genesis 9:25-27, but the card cites only Genesis 9:27.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card is a near-verbatim restatement of Genesis 9:29 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card is a flat list of names and borders with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Stop 2 is the Table of Nations (Genesis 10), a genealogy and so a long stretch. It still has five choice cards: four on the Nimrod aside (10:9-11) and one on the closing summary verse (10:32). The docs say a long stretch never gets a choice card. They also say a stop needs at least as many choice cards as story cards, and they allow naming one standout detail. Here Nimrod gets five cards.
findings.question: Inside a genealogy, does a short narrative aside like Nimrod (10:8-12), or the closing summary verse (10:32), count as part of the long stretch, or can it get choice cards? And when a stop is mostly a long stretch, how should the 'choice cards equal to or more than story cards' rule be met? Options include folding the genealogy into the previous stop or letting the stop fall short.
